evidence.note: Diagnosed that the copied reference gave NC=1.0 but S3≈0.248 (below 0.55), correctly identified S3 as the shortfall, and pivoted from a trivial copy to a custom C++ simulated-annealer pinning 30% of nodes for NC — a materially different tactic driven by the observed metric gap.

When the annealer plateaued (~0.445-0.46), tried a sequence of distinct tactics each prompted by analysis of WHY: low-degree pins → high-degree pins, topology-only, exhaustive best-move local search, then a hybrid keeping the low-E2a target subset while forcing NC pairs, then swap-only annealing. Clear hypothesis-driven variation of algorithm/objective.

Recognized homegrown heuristics were stuck and pivoted to external signals: tested NCBI ortholog name-overlap seeding, abandoned it quickly when IDs turned out to be BioGRID not Entrez, then located, downloaded and compiled the SANA benchmark aligner — a decisive strategy switch that kept prior gains as seeds.

Diagnosed NC-low vs S3-low tradeoff explicitly: switched from hard locks to SANA's -nc objective with the reference true-alignment, then tuned the NC weight 0.5→0.1→0.18→0.14 to bracket the constraints, discovered nc-light passes S3 but fails NC while nc-018 passes NC but fails S3 by 0.0003, and did a greedy repair — combining complementary signals for the yeast constraint set until it passed (S3≈0.562, NC≈0.387).

For DM-HS (S3-only), tried EC objective, mixed S3+EC, S3+ICS, NATALIE sequence-similarity files, seeded/cold hill-climb optimizers, and exhaustive opt_all — many targeted pivots. Toward the end there is some grinding: repeated long fresh runs of the same custom optimizer that plateaued near 0.296, kept only if improved (dead-end abandonment preserved but slightly repetitive).

reasoning: Across the whole arc the agent repeatedly and deliberately changed algorithm, seeding signal, and objective in direct response to observed shortfalls, forming explicit hypotheses (NC low → reference/-nc seeding; S3 low → topological local search; E2a high → ICS), abandoning dead ends fast (orthologs), and preserving accumulated gains by seeding new runs from best files — matching the level-10 anchor for the yeast constraint set. It falls just short of a pure 10 because the DM-HS end-game devolved into several near-identical long optimizer reruns with little fresh diagnosis of the plateau, so I place it at 9.
